items.title: aioscaleway
items.text:
aioscaleway, every Scaleway API in Python, fully async and strongly typed.

Documentation: https://aioscaleway.businessagile.eu

Source Code: https://gitlab.com/businessagile/libraries/aioscaleway

aioscaleway is a client for the Scaleway APIs, organised around what you manipulate (servers, volumes, clusters, invoices) rather than where Scaleway files it. It is async from end to end and strongly typed, and covers every published API, not only the popular ones.

aioscaleway is based on Python type annotations, and powered by Pydantic, httpx2, whenever and stamina.

The key features are:

  • Async first: one HTTP client per Scaleway object, every call awaited. The official scaleway-async package calls requests inside its async def methods and blocks the event loop.
  • Business areas: compute, storage, network, kubernetes, databases, billing... the same areas as its sibling aioovh.
  • References and objects: scw.compute.servers(server_id) acts without reading the server first, await loads it, and a loaded server is still a reference.
  • Collections: async for reads every page, filter() narrows, pages() gives the page totals.
  • One method per action: server.reboot(), server.power_off(), server.attach_volume(volume_id=volume).
  • No API version in any name: the latest stable version of each API, else its latest preview, chosen for you.
  • Complete: generated from the 91 OpenAPI files Scaleway publishes, 59 API versions and about 1,500 operations, each reachable.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
A recent and currently supported version of Python: 3.12 or later.

A Scaleway API key, given as an argument or read from the SCW_* variables of the Scaleway CLI.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
$ pip install aioscaleway
---> 100%
Successfully installed aioscaleway httpx2 pydantic pydantic-settings stamina whenever

items.title: Connect
items.text:
from aioscaleway import Scaleway

scw = Scaleway(
    secret_key="...",
    default_region="fr-par",
    default_zone="fr-par-1",
    default_project_id="...",
)

Every value left out is read from SCW_SECRET_KEY, SCW_DEFAULT_REGION, SCW_DEFAULT_ZONE, SCW_DEFAULT_PROJECT_ID and the other variables of the Scaleway CLI.

items.title: Load, act, iterate
items.text:
async with scw:
    server = await scw.compute.servers(server_id)
    print(server.name, server.state)
    await server.reboot()

    await scw.compute.servers(other_id).power_off()

    async for server in scw.compute.servers.filter(name="web"):
        print(server.id, server.creation_date)

scw.compute.servers(server_id) is a reference: it makes no request. await loads the server, an action runs directly on the reference, and iterating the collection reads every page.

items.title: Sub-resources
items.text:
async for pool in scw.kubernetes.clusters(cluster_id).pools:
    print(pool.name, pool.size)

A pool belongs to its cluster, even though Scaleway serves it at /pools/{pool_id}.

items.title: Billing, with totals
items.text:
consumptions = scw.billing.consumptions.filter(billing_period="2026-10")
async for page in consumptions.pages():
    for line in page.consumptions:
        print(line.sku, line.value.to_decimal() if line.value else 0)
    print("discount", page.total_discount_untaxed_value)

items.title: Editor support everywhere
items.text: Arguments, fields and results are typed, and checked with mypy --strict. Dates are whenever.Instant, amounts Money with .to_decimal(), enumerations are open so that a value Scaleway adds later does not break your code.

items.title: Architecture
items.text: The conventions shared with aioovh are in the Business Agile conventions (backend/08-python-api-clients.md, draft in /opt/businessagile/libraries/conventions-clients-api.md). This file covers what is specific to Scaleway.

items.title: Two layers
items.text:
• Operations (src/aioscaleway/_operations/<product>/<version>/), private: one typed method per OpenAPI operation, models and enums, generated by scripts/operations.py. It follows the API's layout and versions, and changes whenever Scaleway does.
  • Objects (src/aioscaleway/<area>/), public: business areas, collections, references and loaded objects, generated by scripts/objects.py from the operations and mapping.yaml. It changes only when the meaning does.

The hand-written runtime is _client.py (HTTP, authentication, retries), _objects.py (collections, references, binding), _root.py (Scaleway), _settings.py, _errors.py, _models.py and _enums.py.

scripts/generate.py runs both generators. CI fails when src/ or docs/ differ from what they produce.

items.title: How the objects are derived
items.text:
1. Version. For each product API class (instance Api, baremetal PrivateNetworkApi...), the latest stable version, else the latest preview. mapping.yaml versions overrides it: the Elastic Metal private networks stay in v1 to share the v1 server, and the Instance v2alpha1 volume API stays in the operations layer only. Operations of other versions are listed in docs/coverage.md as such.
  2. Resources. A path segment followed by a parameter (/servers/{server_id}) is a resource. The zone or region segment is a scope, not a resource.
  3. Placement of each operation:
  4. on the item path: Get* loads it, PATCH is update, PUT is update or replace (Set*), DELETE is delete, anything else is an action named after the operation without the resource's name (AttachServerVolume on servers gives attach_volume);
  5. on the collection path: List* is the iteration, Create* is create, anything else a collection method;
  6. a List* with no item path becomes an iterable collection without identifiers (scw.billing.consumptions);
  7. a resource whose item path is at the root but whose list is under a parent (/pools/{pool_id}, /clusters/{cluster_id}/pools) belongs to that parent: scw.kubernetes.clusters(cluster_id).pools;
  8. anything else is a method of the area.
  9. Actions with an enum. An operation named *Action whose body has an enum action becomes one method per value: ServerAction gives power_on, power_off, reboot, backup, stop_in_place, terminate, enable_routed_ip.
  10. Loaded classes subclass the operations model and the reference (class Server(_InstanceServer, ServerRef)). When a listing returns a summary model, a ...Summary class plays the same role.
  11. Names. Areas come from mapping.yaml namespaces. Collections take their path segment; collections renames them, and prefixes puts a business prefix in front of a collection whose name another product of the area also uses. members renames actions. The generator stops on any remaining clash, of collections, classes or members, so a name is never chosen silently.

items.title: Identifiers
items.text: A key is a dict of the path parameters a reference needs (server_id, zone). A loaded object rebuilds its key from its fields (id, zone). Integer identifiers (Dedibox) are accepted as int | str. An argument naming another resource (volume_id) accepts a string, a reference or an object.

items.title: Generated models
items.text:
• Field defaults follow proto3: an absent scalar is its zero value; a field the spec requires has no default.
  • Enumerations are open (OpenStrEnum); unknown fields are kept.
  • Dates are whenever.Instant, parsed by whenever's pydantic integration.
  • google.type.Money is the hand-written Money.
  • Every model is rebuilt at the end of its module, so that the loaded classes in another module inherit resolved fields.

items.title: Where the specs come from
items.text: The developers website lists every OpenAPI file in its Zudoku bundle; scripts/spec_index.py extracts the list and scripts/fetch_specs.sh downloads them with curl (the website refuses the default client of Python HTTP libraries), then regenerates.

items.title: Import time
items.text: import aioscaleway loads the runtime only. Each area is imported the first time it is used (scw.compute), since an area holds thousands of models.

items.title: Retries
items.text: Idempotent methods are retried on 429, 502, 503, 504 and transport errors; a POST only on 429, 503 or a connection that never opened.

items.title: Design and roadmap
items.text: aioscaleway is developed in the open. This page states what it aims at, what it leaves out, and what comes next. Discussion happens in the GitLab issues.

items.title: Principles
items.text:
1. Async only. No synchronous twin of the API: one way to do each thing.
  2. Objects, not URLs. The public surface follows what you manipulate; paths and versions are details of the routing, chosen by the library.
  3. Types first. If the type checker cannot follow it, it is not the API.
  4. Everything reachable. Every operation Scaleway publishes is either an object method or explicitly left to the raw layer, and a test keeps it that way.
  5. Generated, then reviewed. The code is generated from Scaleway's OpenAPI files; the names come from rules and from a mapping reviewed in merge requests, and the generator stops rather than guess a name.

items.title: Two layers
items.text:
• Operations (aioscaleway._operations), private: one typed method per OpenAPI operation, following Scaleway's products and versions.
  • Objects (aioscaleway.compute, aioscaleway.billing...), public: business areas, collections, references and loaded objects, generated from the operations and mapping.yaml.

The architecture page details how operations become objects.

items.title: Non goals
items.text:
• A synchronous client.
  • Object Storage: it speaks the S3 protocol, and S3 clients already do it well.
  • Hiding the API: scw.raw reaches any path, and every object method says which call it makes.

items.title: Roadmap
items.text: Step Content 0.1 Every API as objects, collections, references, actions, pages, typed errors, retries 0.2 wait_until(state=...) on resources with a life cycle (servers, clusters, databases) 0.3 References from fields that name another resource, first() and count() where the API allows it 0.4 Documentation examples executed by the test suite, recipes for FastAPI and task workers later A shared core with aioovh, then other European providers

items.title: Prior art
items.text: aioscaleway stands on what others built: the official Scaleway SDK for its OpenAPI files and naming, the Stainless generated SDKs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cloudflare) for the resource tree, hcloud-python for bound objects, and the Azure SDK design guidelines for versions and paging.

items.title: Async down to the socket
items.text:
Scaleway's official SDK comes in two packages, scaleway and scaleway-async, and both send their requests with requests. The async def methods of scaleway-async call it directly, so each request blocks the event loop of a FastAPI application or a task worker while it waits for Scaleway.

aioscaleway keeps one httpx2.AsyncClient per Scaleway object, reuses its connections, and awaits every request. A hundred concurrent calls are a hundred coroutines, not a hundred threads.

items.title: Business objects, not URLs
items.text:
Scaleway's APIs are organised by product and version: /instance/v1/zones/{zone}/servers, /k8s/v1/regions/{region}/pools/{pool_id}. The official SDK mirrors them, one class per product and version (InstanceV1API, BillingV2Beta1API).

aioscaleway exposes what you manipulate instead:

You write You get Requests scw.compute.servers a collection none scw.compute.servers.filter(name="web") the same collection, narrowed none async for s in scw.compute.servers loaded objects one per page scw.compute.servers(server_id) a reference none await scw.compute.servers(server_id) a loaded object one await scw.compute.servers(server_id).reboot() the action's result one await scw.compute.servers.create(...) the created object one

A loaded object is a reference too: anything that takes a reference takes an object. A reference does not load itself when printed or read, because those are synchronous; mypy flags a field read on a bare reference, and repr() tells which one you hold.

The full tree, with every collection and action, is on the object tree page.

items.title: Strongly typed, end to end
items.text:
• Every argument, field and result is typed, and the package is checked with mypy --strict in CI.
  • Responses are Pydantic models. Dates are whenever.Instant, amounts Money with .to_decimal().
  • Enumerations are open: a status or a commercial type Scaleway adds after a release is accepted, instead of failing the whole response.
  • An argument naming another resource (volume_id) takes a string, a reference or an object.

items.title: Versions out of sight
items.text: No class, module or attribute carries an API version. For each API, aioscaleway uses the latest stable version, and the latest preview when there is no stable one yet: 28 of the 53 products, including IAM, billing and domains, only exist in preview. A preview operation says so in its docstring.

items.title: Reliable by default
items.text: Throttling (429) and transient failures (502, 503, 504, broken connections) are retried with stamina, honouring Retry-After. A POST is only retried when Scaleway cannot have processed it, so a creation is never sent twice. API errors are typed (ResourceNotFoundError, QuotasExceededError, TransientStateError...) and keep Scaleway's message.

items.title: Complete
items.text: The code is generated from the OpenAPI files Scaleway publishes, committed in the repository: 59 API versions and about 1,500 operations. Every operation is reachable, through the objects or through scw.raw, and the coverage page says where.

items.title: What your browser stores
items.text:

  • The star and fork counts of the repository shown in the header, in sessionStorage (__source), so they are fetched once per visit.

Neither leaves your browser.

items.title: Who receives your requests
items.text:
• GitLab Pages (GitLab Inc., United States) serves every page and, like any web server, receives your IP address and browser details with each request.
  • The GitLab API (gitlab.com, GitLab Inc.) answers the two requests your browser sends for the repository shown in the header (its star and fork counts, and its latest release), and receives your IP address with them.

See the GitLab privacy statement.
